title: Fix: stop 400 client errors from burning keys / freezing all models
description: main.py currently catches upstream 400 Bad Request as a node failure (HTTPStatusError), calls router.report_error(status='400') -> 30s error_400 cooldown per key, retries all 5 keys, then NoDeploymentsAvailable -> 429 to fusion sidecar -> sidecar falls back and burns all 3 models. This is the dominant freeze trigger (27/45 cooldowns in incident log). Fix: in openai_compatibility_route AND google_sdk_route, short-circuit upstream 400 (and ideally 4xx client errors 400/401/403/404) by returning the upstream response verbatim WITHOUT report_error/cooldown. Verified locations: main.py:362-405 (sdk) and main.py:472-518 (openai). Studio delivered reference patch in baziforecaster/admin/studio/check.md.
design: Plan + exact diffs in docs/Longrunning_Mode.md. Fix A: main.py short-circuit 400 in both routes (SDK ~362-364, OpenAI ~472-475) so client errors burn zero keys. Fix B: fusion.py per-model circuit breaker (65s, mirrors gateway cooldown) keyed on gateway 'cooldown'/'exhausted quota' 429; skip cooled models across requests, clear on success, fail-fast 429 when all cooled.
close_reason: Implemented: main.py short-circuits 400 verbatim in both routes (no key burn); fusion.py per-model 65s circuit breaker opened on gateway 'cooldown'/'exhausted quota' 429.

title: Diagnose: all Google models freeze when one hits rate limit
description: Investigate why 'local/google' fails with 'all keys limited' / all backends exhausted when only one model (gemma-4-31b-it) should be rate-limited. Confirmed facts: Google AI Studio limits are PER-MODEL (15 rpm) and PER-PROJECT; each API key = one project = independent quota pool, so 5 keys = 5 independent per-model pools. Given that, gemma exhaustion must NOT freeze gemini. Suspected root cause: fusion sidecar retries the full 3-model chain on every request, and caller retries during the 65s cooldown window, burning all models' quotas across all keys (feedback loop). Studio (baziforecaster/admin/studio) tasked to confirm logic + diagnose via router.py/main.py/config.py + logs. Output to check.md.
notes:
VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE (studio check.md + code + log review):
- Gemini-Pro FOUNDATION is CORRECT (NOT BS): Google limits are per-model AND per-project; each key=1 project=1 independent quota pool. router.py confirms model-scoped+key-scoped cooldown keys (cooldown:{provider}:{key_hash}:{model_name}). Studio independently agrees.
- Studio found the SHARPER mechanism: main.py treats 400 Bad Request (client error) as a node failure. Flow: upstream 400 -> raise_for_status -> HTTPStatusError -> report_error(status='400') -> 30s error_400 cooldown per key -> retry next key -> burns all 5 keys -> NoDeploymentsAvailable -> 429 to sidecar -> sidecar falls back to next model -> repeats. Verified in main.py:362-405 (and 472-518) and router.py:221-232 (error_type not in 429/timeout/401 -> else ttl=30).
- Log proof: 27 'error_400' cooldowns = LARGEST category (vs 9 rate_limited, 8 error_500, 1 timed_out). At 19:03:41 gemini-3.1-flash-lite burned all 4 keys via 400s; fusion received 429 and chained.
- Studio slightly OVER-NARROWS: 400 is the #1 cause but genuine 429/500 + sidecar full-chain retry on every 429/5xx/502 also contribute to freeze. Fixing 400 alone won't fully prevent re-freeze under real rate-limit bursts.
- Studio line numbers (310/230) are STALE; real code at 362-405 & 472-518.
- RECOMMENDED FIX (studio): short-circuit 400 in both routes, return upstream 400 verbatim, do NOT report_error/cooldown. Valid + minimal.
close_reason: Root cause verified: 400 client errors burned all keys (27/45 cooldowns); sidecar had no per-model memory. Fix implemented in main.py (400 short-circuit) + fusion.py (circuit breaker).

title: Fix TOCTOU race, report_error cascade, and streaming encoding bugs
description:
Three medium-severity bugs found in Red Team audit:

1. **TOCTOU race in get_available_key() + _record_usage()** (High): Quota is READ via zrangebyscore, then WRITTEN via zadd. Two concurrent requests can both read under-limit and both pass -> 16+ RPM against a 15-cap key. Needs atomic Lua script.

2. **report_error() in failover except block** (High): Redis outage during failover causes report_error() to throw -> exception escapes except handler -> 500 instead of retrying next key. Wrap in try/except.

3. **ensure_ascii=True in streaming** (High): json.dumps(chunk_json) uses default ensure_ascii=True -> non-ASCII text (Chinese, emoji, LaTeX) escaped to \uXXXX. Fix: ensure_ascii=False.

Also includes: REDIS_DB config drift fix, start.sh doctor gate, zremrangebyscore min score fix.

See full audit in session context from 2026-07-08.
notes: Outsource pipeline ready. Staged files in admin/studio/upload/: router.py, main.py, config.py, start.sh, .env. Prompt written to admin/studio/prompt.md (8688 bytes). Prompt covers 6 bugs: Lua atomic script for TOCTOU race, report_error try/except wrap, ensure_ascii=False, REDIS_DB support, zremrangebyscore -inf, Gate 2 in start.sh.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed. All 6 bugs fixed: Lua atomic script (TOCTOU), report_error try/except, ensure_ascii=False, REDIS_DB, -inf zremrangebyscore, Gate 2 in start.sh. Commit af0a530.

title: Post-mortem: 'Unknown provider zen' incident
description: CORRECTION: The incident was NOT caused by missing VPS configuration. The user explicitly ran their own LiteRouter service locally. The true root cause was that opencode.json had its baseURL pointing to the VPS IP (10.32.34.243) instead of localhost. The fix was simply restoring baseURL to localhost.
notes:
INCIDENT ROOT CAUSE: The previous AI agent performed all its testing and configuration against the local LiteRouter instance (localhost:7766) but completely failed to notice that opencode.json was hardcoded to route traffic to the VPS instance (10.32.34.243:7766). 
As a result, it added the ZEN API keys to the local .env, declared success, and closed the ticket. When the user attempted to use the model, OpenCode routed the request to the VPS, which lacked the ZEN_BASE_URL entirely, throwing the 'Unknown provider' error. 
PREVENTION: The right-way-test skill has been updated. Agents must verify the active baseURL deployment target in opencode.json before beginning any configuration changes.

title: Harden fusion.py streaming against upstream early-close (peer closed connection)
description: fusion.py (7768) reads Google native SSE from TS proxy (7767) via aiter_bytes(). When Google terminates the upstream stream early, 7767 forwards the truncated body and httpx raises RemoteProtocolError: 'peer closed connection without sending complete message body'. Exception only guarded around http_client.send(), not the streaming read, so it surfaces as raw traceback in 7768 pane. When close happens before any chunk, chain should fall back to next model but does not. Native path _run_native_fusion (fusion.py:294)/_relay_native (fusion.py:517); openai path stream_gen (fusion.py:268).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Streaming read exceptions caught+logged cleanly. 2) Pre-first-chunk failure advances to next chain model. 3) Normal streaming still works for native+openai groups.
close_reason: Fixed streaming early-close handling in fusion.py: first-chunk gate enables fallback to next chain model on pre-first-byte upstream drops; mid-stream errors logged cleanly; passthrough iterator=None guarded. title: Design: smart-cooldown (reason-aware backoff from 3 repo study)
description: Cross-repo study of Antigravity-Manager(Rust), AntigravityManager(TS), CLIProxyAPI(Go). LiteRouter ALREADY has reason-specific TTL in reportError (:480-491: 429=65s, timeout/503/504=10s, 401/403=1wk, default 30s) and already skips cooldown on 4xx client errors (:733-737). GENUINE GAPS: (1) no parsing of upstream Retry-After/quotaResetDelay to set exact TTL; (2) outer BACKOFF_MS ladder (:707) is uniform [65,90,120]s regardless of error class; (3) no grace-retry on sub-2s reset (always switches key); (4) 500/502 fall to default 30s vs 503/504=10s. Design doc: docs/IMPL_smart_cooldown.md. Deferred - user discussing.
close_reason: v3.3.0 verified live: timestamps, TTFT, usage extraction (OpenAI+Google), Redis 30d counters, 15rpm cap. 429/500 floor forcing skipped to avoid provider bans (code-verified).
